title: Intent Object
description: Schema for the Intent object produced by Phase 1 (Intent Compilation). Captures the raw request, parsed objective, constraints, consequence level, and output requirements that drive all downstream phases.

metadata.description: Tracking metadata for the intent compilation.

project_id.description: Unique identifier for the project. Format: kebab-case slug derived from the project name.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the intent was compiled.

intent.description: The parsed and enriched representation of the user's build request.

raw_request.description: The original, unmodified request as provided by the human operator.
examples: Build a multi-tenant SaaS platform for project management with real-time collaboration, Gantt charts, and Jira integration.

objective.description: A single, clear sentence that captures what the system must achieve. Distilled from the raw request by the intent analyst.
examples: Deliver a multi-tenant SaaS project management platform with real-time collaboration, visual scheduling, and third-party tool integration.

desired_outcomes.description: Concrete, measurable outcomes that define success for this project. Each outcome should be testable.
examples: Users can create and manage projects with task hierarchies
Bi-directional sync with Jira via REST API

known_constraints.description: Constraints explicitly stated by the requester (budget, timeline, technology mandates, compliance requirements, etc.).
examples: Must use PostgreSQL as primary database

implicit_constraints.description: Constraints inferred by the intent analyst that were not explicitly stated but are logically necessary (e.g., multi-tenancy implies tenant isolation).
examples: Multi-tenancy requires strict data isolation between tenants
Real-time collaboration requires WebSocket or SSE infrastructure
Jira integration requires OAuth 2.0 token management

consequence_level.description: The assessed severity level of getting this system wrong. Drives risk tolerance, audit depth, and escalation thresholds.

ambiguity_notes.description: Areas where the request is ambiguous or underspecified. These are NOT blockers but are recorded for downstream phases to resolve or escalate.
examples: Unclear whether 'real-time collaboration' means CRDT-based or OT-based
No mention of mobile support — assumed web-only unless clarified
Pricing model not specified — affects tenant provisioning design

domain_signals.description: Domain-specific signals detected in the request that influence architectural decisions (e.g., regulatory domains, industry verticals, scale indicators).
examples: B2B SaaS — implies enterprise SSO, audit logging, role-based access
Project management domain — implies complex state machines for task lifecycle
Jira integration — implies familiarity with Atlassian ecosystem

system_type_classification.description: The classified system type that determines which build workflow the Commander selects. Must match a registered workflow in the OS manifest.

output_requirements.description: Specifies what artifacts the build must produce and how they should be delivered.

required_artifacts.description: List of artifact types that must be produced by the build pipeline.

format_preferences.description: Preferred formats for output artifacts (e.g., OpenAPI 3.1, Terraform, Helm charts).

handoff_targets.description: Downstream consumers of the build output (teams, systems, CI pipelines, etc.).
